name: Simon
overview: Simon was a male individual known as the tanner with whom the Apostle Peter stayed in Joppa. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. Simon's role is briefly noted in the Book of Acts, highlighting his connection to Peter during a significant moment in the early church.
namesAndTitles: The name Simon means 'he has heard' or 'obedient one' in the original language. This proper name does not appear to have been given by God specifically but reflects a common Hebrew or Greek name of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Simon beyond his association as the tanner with whom Peter stayed. No further relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Simon’s significance lies in his hospitality toward Peter, providing a place for the apostle to stay in Joppa. This setting is important in the narrative of Acts 9:43, where Peter's ministry is expanding beyond Jewish boundaries. Simon’s role, though brief, supports the unfolding of God’s plan through Peter’s missionary work.
